nodes.text: If $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is such that $A+A$ contains all but finitely many integers then $\limsup 1_A\ast 1_A(n)=\infty$.

#28 : [ErTu41] [Er56] [Er57] [Er59] [Er61] [Er65] [Er65b] [Er69] [Er70c] [Er73] [Er77c] [Er80,p.98] [ErGr80] [Er81] [Er85c] [Er89d] [Er90] [Er94b] [Er95] [Er97c] [Er97f] [Va99,1.16] number theory | additive basis Conjectured by Erdős and Turán. They also suggest the stronger conjecture that $\limsup 1_A\ast 1_A(n)/\log n>0$. Another stronger conjecture would be that the hypothesis $\lvert A\cap [1,N]\rvert \gg N^{1/2}$ for all large $N$ suffices. See also [40] , and [1145] for a stronger generalisation. This is discussed in problem C9 of Guy's collection [Gu04] .
